# 12-Week Post-MI Cardiac-Safe Fitness Programme

## Client Profile & Constraints
- Age: 58 years
- Status: 6 months post-MI, cardiac rehab cleared
- HR ceiling: 115 bpm (70% age-predicted max)
- Restrictions: Moderate intensity only, no Valsalva manoeuvre, no maximal lifts
- Setting: Full gym access
- Goal: Safe return to general fitness, cardiovascular stability, functional strength

---

## Programme Overview

This 12-week plan uses three 4-week phases with progressive complexity and volume. Each week includes 3 supervised sessions (ideally with you present for monitoring). The emphasis is on steady-state aerobic work, controlled resistance with higher reps/lower loads, and consistent HR management.

**Key Principles:**
- RPE 4–6/10 (moderate, conversational intensity)
- HR monitoring at session start, mid-point, and end
- 2–3 minutes rest between sets
- Breathing cues to prevent Valsalva (exhale on exertion)
- No straining, no breath-holding

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation & Acclimatisation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goals:** Establish baseline fitness, build confidence, normalise gym environment, develop movement patterns with light loads.

### Weekly Structure
- **Session A:** Aerobic base + lower-body mobility
- **Session B:** Upper-body light resistance + steady cardio
- **Session C:** Mixed-modality aerobic + core stability

Minimum 48 hours between sessions. Sessions last 40–50 minutes.

---

### **Week 1**

#### Session A (Monday) – Aerobic Base + Lower Mobility
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 2 min easy walking on treadmill (RPE 2–3)
- 3 min dynamic leg swings, arm circles, torso rotations

**Main (30 min):**
- Stationary bike: 20 min steady state, HR target 100–110 bpm
  - Resistance: light (RPE 4/10)
  - Cadence: 80–90 rpm
  - Check HR every 5 min; adjust resistance if HR creeps above 115
- Walking lunges (bodyweight): 2 × 8 per leg, slow and controlled
- Glute bridges: 2 × 10, 2-second hold at top

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Easy walking, 2 min
- Seated hamstring stretch, quad stretch, hip flexor stretch (30 sec each side)

---

#### Session B (Wednesday) – Upper-Body Light Resistance + Steady Cardio
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 2 min treadmill walk
- Arm circles, band pull-aparts (2 × 10)

**Main (35 min):**
- Treadmill walk: 10 min, HR 100–110 bpm
- Dumbbell chest press (seated on bench): 2 × 12 reps @ 4–5 kg per hand
  - Controlled descent (2 sec), exhale on press
  - Rest 2 min between sets
- Dumbbell rows (seated, single-arm): 2 × 10 per side @ 4–5 kg
  - Exhale as you pull
  - Rest 2 min
- Lat pulldown (light stack): 2 × 12 @ 20–25 kg
  - Exhale as you pull down
  - Rest 2 min
- Treadmill walk: 5 min cool-down, HR dropping toward 90 bpm

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Chest stretch, shoulder stretch, tricep stretch (30 sec each)

---

#### Session C (Friday) – Mixed Aerobic + Core
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 2 min easy elliptical
- Bodyweight squats × 10, arm swings

**Main (35 min):**
- Elliptical: 15 min steady, HR 100–110 bpm, RPE 4/10
- Plank hold (on knees): 2 × 20 sec, rest 1 min
- Dead bugs: 2 × 8 per side, slow and controlled
- Bird dogs: 2 × 8 per side
- Elliptical: 10 min, HR dropping to 95–105 bpm
- Glute bridges: 2 × 12

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Seated spinal twist, child's pose, deep breathing

---

### **Week 2**

Repeat Week 1 structure but with minor progressions:
- **Bike/elliptical/treadmill:** Increase duration by 2–3 min (e.g., bike 22 min instead of 20)
- **Resistance exercises:** Add 1 rep to each set (e.g., 2 × 13 instead of 2 × 12)
- **Dumbbell weight:** If RPE was 3/10, increase to 5–6 kg per hand
- **Core holds:** Increase plank to 25 sec

**Monitoring:** Client should report any chest discomfort, unusual breathlessness, or dizziness immediately. HR should remain ≤115 bpm throughout.

---

### **Week 3**

Further progression:
- **Aerobic duration:** +2–3 min per session (bike 25 min, elliptical 17 min, treadmill 12 min)
- **Resistance reps:** 2 × 14 across all upper-body exercises
- **Dumbbell weight:** 6–7 kg per hand if tolerated
- **Core:** Plank 30 sec, add side plank (on knees) 2 × 15 sec per side

**New exercise (Session B):** Seated shoulder press with light dumbbells (2 × 10 @ 4 kg), emphasising exhale on press.

---

### **Week 4 – Consolidation**

Maintain Week 3 volumes but refine movement quality:
- Reduce rest periods slightly (2 min → 90 sec) if HR recovery is good
- Add one extra set to one exercise per session (e.g., chest press 3 × 12)
- Introduce light resistance band work: bicep curls (2 × 12) and tricep extensions (2 × 12) in Session B

**Assessment point:** By end of Week 4, client should comfortably sustain 25 min aerobic work at HR 100–110 bpm with RPE 4/10, and perform 2–3 sets of 12–14 reps with light dumbbells without discomfort.

---

## PHASE 2: Progressive Strength & Aerobic Capacity (Weeks 5–8)

**Goals:** Increase resistance load and aerobic duration, introduce more compound patterns, build muscular endurance.

### Weekly Structure
- **Session A:** Lower-body strength + aerobic finisher
- **Session B:** Upper-body push/pull + steady cardio
- **Session C:** Full-body circuit + aerobic base

---

### **Week 5**

#### Session A (Monday) – Lower-Body Strength + Aerobic Finisher
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 3 min treadmill walk
- Bodyweight squats × 12, leg swings × 10 per leg

**Main (40 min):**
- Leg press (light stack): 3 × 12 @ 40–50 kg
  - Controlled descent (2 sec), exhale on press
  - Rest 2 min between sets
  - HR check after set 2
- Leg extension (light): 2 × 12 @ 30–40 kg
  - Rest 90 sec
- Hamstring curl (light): 2 × 12 @ 25–35 kg
  - Rest 90 sec
- Stationary bike: 10 min aerobic finisher, HR 105–115 bpm, RPE 5/10

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Quad stretch, hamstring stretch, hip flexor stretch (45 sec each)

---

#### Session B (Wednesday) – Upper-Body Push/Pull + Steady Cardio
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 2 min treadmill walk
- Band pull-aparts × 12, arm circles

**Main (40 min):**
- Treadmill walk: 12 min, HR 100–110 bpm
- Dumbbell bench press (incline bench): 3 × 12 @ 7–8 kg per hand
  - Rest 2 min
- Dumbbell rows (standing, alternating): 3 × 10 per side @ 7–8 kg
  - Rest 2 min
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 12 @ 30–35 kg
  - Rest 90 sec
- Seated shoulder press: 2 × 12 @ 5–6 kg per hand
  - Rest 90 sec
- Treadmill walk: 5 min cool-down

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Chest, shoulder, and tricep stretches

---

#### Session C (Friday) – Full-Body Circuit + Aerobic Base
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 3 min elliptical
- Bodyweight squats, arm swings, torso rotations

**Main (40 min):**
- Elliptical: 15 min steady, HR 100–110 bpm
- Circuit (2 rounds, 90 sec rest between rounds):
  - Goblet squats (light dumbbell): 10 reps @ 6 kg
  - Dumbbell chest press (standing): 10 reps @ 6 kg per hand
  - Glute bridges: 12 reps
  - Dumbbell rows (single-arm): 8 per side @ 6 kg
  - Plank hold: 30 sec
- Elliptical: 8 min cool-down, HR 95–105 bpm

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Full-body stretching

---

### **Week 6**

Progression from Week 5:
- **Aerobic duration:** +2–3 min (treadmill 14 min, bike 12 min, elliptical 17 min)
- **Resistance sets:** Add one set to leg press and bench press (3 → 4 sets)
- **Dumbbell weight:** 8–9 kg per hand if RPE was 4/10
- **Circuit:** Increase to 3 rounds, reduce rest to 75 sec between rounds
- **New exercise (Session A):** Calf raises (bodyweight or light dumbbell) 2 × 15

---

### **Week 7**

Further progression:
- **Aerobic:** Treadmill 15 min, bike 13 min, elliptical 18 min
- **Resistance reps:** Increase to 3 × 13 or 4 × 12 across main lifts
- **Dumbbell weight:** 9–10 kg per hand
- **Circuit:** 3 rounds, 60 sec rest, add one new exercise (e.g., lateral raises 2 × 10 @ 4 kg)
- **Core:** Introduce dead bug with light dumbbell hold (2 × 10 per side)

---

### **Week 8 – Consolidation**

Maintain Week 7 volumes with focus on consistency:
- Reduce rest periods further (2 min → 90 sec on main lifts) if HR recovery is good
- Increase circuit rounds to 4 if tolerated, reduce rest to 60 sec
- Add light resistance band work: lateral walks (2 × 12 per direction)

**Assessment point:** By end of Week 8, client should sustain 15 min aerobic work at HR 105–115 bpm with RPE 5/10, and perform 3–4 sets of 12–13 reps with 8–10 kg dumbbells comfortably.

---

## PHASE 3: Maintenance & Functional Integration (Weeks 9–12)

**Goals:** Consolidate gains, introduce functional movement patterns, prepare for independent training, maintain cardiac safety.

### Weekly Structure
- **Session A:** Lower-body functional + aerobic
- **Session B:** Upper-body functional + steady cardio
- **Session C:** Full-body functional circuit + aerobic

---

### **Week 9**

#### Session A (Monday) – Lower-Body Functional + Aerobic
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 3 min treadmill walk
- Bodyweight squats × 12, walking lunges × 8 per leg

**Main (45 min):**
- Stationary bike: 12 min warm-up, HR 100–110 bpm
- Goblet squats: 3 × 12 @ 8 kg
  - Rest 2 min
- Walking lunges (with light dumbbells): 3 × 10 per leg @ 5 kg per hand
  - Rest 2 min
- Leg press: 3 × 12 @ 60 kg
  - Rest 90 sec
- Hamstring curl: 2 × 12 @ 40 kg
  - Rest 90 sec
- Calf raises: 2 × 15 (bodyweight)
- Stationary bike: 8 min aerobic finisher, HR 110–115 bpm

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Full lower-body stretching

---

#### Session B (Wednesday) – Upper-Body Functional + Steady Cardio
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 2 min treadmill walk
- Band pull-aparts × 12, arm circles

**Main (45 min):**
- Treadmill walk: 12 min, HR 100–110 bpm
- Dumbbell bench press (incline): 3 × 12 @ 9 kg per hand
  - Rest 2 min
- Dumbbell rows (standing, alternating): 3 × 12 per side @ 9 kg
  - Rest 2 min
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 12 @ 40 kg
  - Rest 90 sec
- Seated shoulder press: 3 × 10 @ 6 kg per hand
  - Rest 90 sec
- Bicep curls (dumbbell): 2 × 12 @ 6 kg per hand
- Tricep extensions (dumbbell): 2 × 12 @ 6 kg per hand
- Treadmill walk: 5 min cool-down

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Upper-body stretching

---

#### Session C (Friday) – Full-Body Functional Circuit + Aerobic
**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 3 min elliptical
- Bodyweight squats, arm swings, torso rotations

**Main (45 min):**
- Elliptical: 15 min steady, HR 100–110 bpm
- Circuit (3 rounds, 60 sec rest between rounds):
  - Goblet squats: 12 reps @ 8 kg
  - Dumbbell chest press (standing): 12 reps @ 8 kg per hand
  - Glute bridges: 15 reps
  - Dumbbell rows (single-arm): 10 per side @ 8 kg
  - Plank hold: 40 sec
  - Lateral raises: 10 reps @ 5 kg per hand
- Elliptical: 8 min cool-down, HR 95–105 bpm

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Full-body stretching

---

### **Week 10**

Progression from Week 9:
- **Aerobic duration:** +2 min (bike 14 min, treadmill 14 min, elliptical 17 min)
- **Resistance sets:** Maintain 3 sets on main lifts, increase reps to 13 if possible
- **Dumbbell weight:** 10 kg per hand on bench/rows if RPE was 4/10
- **Circuit:** 4 rounds, 60 sec rest
- **New exercise (Session B):** Face pulls (light cable or band) 2 × 12

---

### **Week 11**

Further progression:
- **Aerobic:** Bike 15 min, treadmill 15 min, elliptical 18 min
- **Resistance reps:** 3 × 13 or 4 × 12 across main lifts

### Nutrition
- **Meal timing:** Light meal 2–3 hours before session; small snack (banana, toast) 30–45 min before if needed
- **Hydration:** 500 ml water 2 hours pre-session; 200–300 ml every 15 min during session; 500 ml post-session
- **Post-session:** Protein + carbohydrate within 30–60 min (e.g., chicken & rice, Greek yoghurt & berries, protein shake)

- **Sodium:** Maintain normal intake; no restriction unless advised by cardiologist

### Recovery
- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours nightly; consistent bedtime
- **Between sessions:** 48 hours minimum; light activity (walking, stretching) acceptable on off-days
- **Stress management:** Deep breathing, meditation, or relaxation techniques daily
- **Monitoring:** Keep a simple log of HR, RPE, and any symptoms (chest discomfort, unusual breathlessness, palpitations)

## Safety Monitoring & Progression Rules

### HR Monitoring Protocol
- **Pre-session:** Resting HR (should be <80 bpm)
- **During:** Check HR every 5 min during aerobic work; every 2 sets during resistance
- **Post-session:** HR should drop to <100 bpm within 5 min of stopping exercise
- **Recovery:** HR should return to within 10 bpm of resting within 10 min

### Red Flags – Stop Exercise & Seek Medical Advice
- Chest pain or pressure
- Severe breathlessness (unable to speak)
- Dizziness or lightheadedness
- Palpitations or irregular heartbeat
- Nausea or sweating
- HR exceeding 120 bpm during moderate-intensity work
- Unusual fatigue or malaise

### Progression Rules
- Increase load, reps, or duration only if:
  - Previous week completed without symptoms
  - HR response is appropriate (stays ≤115 bpm)
  - RPE remains 4–6/10
  - Recovery is good (HR drops quickly post-session)
- If any session feels unusually hard, repeat that week before progressing
- If symptoms occur, revert to previous week and consult cardiologist

Your client's perception of weakness is common post-MI and reflects:

- **Medication effects:** Beta-blockers can blunt exercise response and perceived exertion

**Evidence supports progressive resistance training post-MI** (within HR/intensity limits) to:

- Enhance metabolic health and glucose control
- Support cardiovascular stability through improved autonomic tone

Your client's desire to lose weight is appropriate post-MI, as:
- **Excess weight increases cardiac workload** and recurrent event risk
- **Weight loss improves:** Blood pressure, lipid profile, insulin sensitivity, exercise capacity

- **Longer steady-state sessions** (25–40 min)
- **Interval training** (moderate-intensity intervals, not high-intensity)
- **Mixed modalities** (bike, treadmill, elliptical, rowing)
- **Increased weekly frequency** (5 sessions/week instead of 4)

# HIIT Integration for Post-MI Client (Phases 2–3)

## Critical Considerations for HIIT Post-MI

**HIIT (High-Intensity Interval Training) is NOT contraindicated post-MI**, but requires careful progression and strict safety parameters:

### Why HIIT Can Be Beneficial:
- **Superior cardiovascular adaptation:** Greater improvements in VO₂ max and cardiac function vs. steady-state alone
- **Time-efficient:** Achieves fitness gains in shorter sessions (20–30 min vs. 40–50 min)
- **Metabolic benefits:** Enhanced fat oxidation, improved insulin sensitivity, greater EPOC (excess post-exercise oxygen consumption)
- **Psychological:** Variety reduces boredom; sense of achievement from high-intensity work

### Why HIIT Requires Caution Post-MI:
- **Arrhythmia risk:** Sudden HR spikes can trigger ectopic beats or arrhythmias in some patients
- **Myocardial demand:** High intensity increases oxygen demand; must ensure coronary perfusion adequate
- **Autonomic stress:** Sympathetic surge during HIIT; beta-blockers may blunt response
- **Valsalva temptation:** Clients may hold breath during hard efforts (contraindicated)

### Safety Criteria for HIIT Introduction:

**Client must meet ALL of the following before HIIT:**
1. ✓ **6+ months post-MI** (your client is at 6 months—borderline acceptable)
2. ✓ **Cardiac rehab clearance** (confirmed in your brief)
3. ✓ **Stress test completed** (ideally; assess with cardiologist if not done)
4. ✓ **Stable on medications** (no recent dose changes)
5. ✓ **No arrhythmias** on recent ECG or Holter monitor
6. ✓ **Sustained 30+ min aerobic work** at HR 100–110 bpm without symptoms (achieved by Week 8)
7. ✓ **Good HR recovery:** HR drops ≥12 bpm within 1 min of stopping exercise
8. ✓ **No angina, dyspnoea, or dizziness** during moderate-intensity intervals (Week 5–8)
9. ✓ **Demonstrated breathing control:** Can maintain rhythmic breathing; no Valsalva tendency
10. ✓ **Cardiologist approval** for HIIT-style training (recommend written clearance)

## Modified HIIT Protocol for Post-MI: "Cardiac-Safe HIIT"

### Key Differences from Standard HIIT:

| **Parameter** | **Standard HIIT** | **Cardiac-Safe HIIT (Post-MI)** |
|---------------|------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Work intensity** | 85–95% max HR (VO₂ max efforts) | 75–85% max HR (hard but not maximal) |
| **Work duration** | 20–60 sec | 60–120 sec (longer efforts, lower peak HR) |
| **Recovery duration** | 20–60 sec | 90–180 sec (longer recovery, fuller HR drop) |
| **Work:recovery ratio** | 1:1 or 1:2 | 1:2 or 1:3 (more conservative) |
| **Number of intervals** | 6–10 | 4–6 (lower volume) |
| **Session frequency** | 2–3/week | 1/week (maximum) |
| **HR ceiling** | 90–95% max HR | 75–85% max HR (≤120 bpm for 58-year-old) |
| **Breathing cue** | Intense, rapid | Rhythmic, controlled; exhale on hard effort |

# Enhanced Strength Programme: Compound Lifts Integration

## Rationale for Compound Lifts Post-MI

Your client's desire for compound movements (squats, deadlifts) is excellent for:
- **Functional strength:** Multi-joint movements mimic real-world activities (standing, lifting, bending)
- **Metabolic benefit:** Larger muscle groups engaged = greater caloric expenditure and hormonal response
- **Efficiency:** Compound lifts achieve more work in less time
- **Confidence:** Mastering heavy, fundamental movements boosts psychological resilience post-MI

### Safety Considerations for Deadlifts & Squats Post-MI:
- **Valsalva risk:** Heavy compound lifts tempt breath-holding; must enforce strict breathing protocol
- **Intra-abdominal pressure:** Deadlifts increase pressure; must use controlled breathing
- **HR spike:** Compound lifts cause larger HR increases; must stay ≤120 bpm
- **Load progression:** Must be gradual; no maximal attempts
- **Form priority:** Perfect technique essential before load increases

### Modified Approach:
- **Lighter loads:** 50–70% of estimated 1RM (not heavy strength work)
- **Higher reps:** 10–15 reps per set (muscular endurance, not maximal strength)
- **Controlled tempo:** 2-sec eccentric, 1-sec pause, 1-sec concentric
- **Breathing cue:** "Exhale on exertion; never hold breath"
- **Rest periods:** 2–3 min between sets (allow full HR recovery)

# Complete 12-Week Post-MI Fitness Programme
## Strength + Cardio + 5K Time Trial + Weight Loss

---

## CLIENT PROFILE & CONSTRAINTS

- **Age:** 58 years
- **Status:** 6 months post-MI, cardiac rehab cleared
- **HR ceiling:** 115 bpm (70% age-predicted max); HIIT ceiling 120 bpm
- **Restrictions:** Moderate intensity only, no Valsalva manoeuvre, no maximal lifts
- **Goals:** 
  - Restore strength and confidence
  - Lose 5–10 kg (0.5–1 kg/week)
  - Build aerobic capacity to complete 5K time trial
  - Improve functional fitness and independence
- **Setting:** Full gym access
- **Medical clearance:** Cardiologist approval for HIIT (Week 9+) required

---

## PROGRAMME OVERVIEW

**Structure:** 3 phases × 4 weeks = 12 weeks total

**Weekly Sessions:** 6 per week (3 strength, 3 cardio)
- **Monday:** Strength A (Lower-body compounds)
- **Tuesday:** Cardio 1 (Steady-state or 5K tempo)
- **Wednesday:** Strength B (Upper-body compounds)
- **Thursday:** Cardio 2 (Intervals or HIIT)
- **Friday:** Strength C (Full-body compounds + metabolic)
- **Saturday:** Cardio 3 (Long steady-state or 5K build)
- **Sunday:** Rest or light activity (optional)

**Key Principles:**
- RPE 4–6/10 (moderate, conversational intensity)
- HR monitoring at session start, mid-point, and end
- 2–3 minutes rest between strength sets
- Breathing cues to prevent Valsalva (exhale on exertion)
- No straining, no breath-holding
- Progressive overload: +1 rep or +5 kg per week
- Nutrition: 1,600–1,700 kcal/day with 1.6–2.0 g protein/kg

---

# PHASE 1: WEEKS 1–4 – FOUNDATION STRENGTH & AEROBIC BASE

**Goals:** Learn compound movement patterns; establish baseline strength; build aerobic foundation; develop confidence; initiate weight loss.

---

## WEEK 1

### Session A (Monday) – Lower-Body Compounds + Core

**Duration:** 55 min | **Intensity:** Moderate (RPE 5/10)

**Warm-up (10 min):**
- 3 min treadmill walk (RPE 2–3, HR 85–90 bpm)
- 10 bodyweight squats (slow, controlled)
- 10 glute bridges
- 10 leg swings per leg
- 5 cat-cow stretches
- 5 inchworms
- Arm circles, torso rotations

**Main (40 min):**

**1. Barbell Back Squat (Primary Lower-Body Compound)**

*Setup:* High bar position across upper traps; shoulder-width stance; toes slightly out (10–15°); parallel or slightly below depth.

*Breathing:* Inhale at top; exhale forcefully on drive-up; NEVER hold breath.

*Tempo:* 2 sec down, 1 sec pause, 1 sec up.

**Warm-up sets:**
- 1 × 8 @ 45 kg (empty bar)
- 1 × 6 @ 50 kg
- 1 × 4 @ 55 kg

**Working sets:**
- 4 sets × 10 reps @ 60 kg
- Rest 2.5 min between sets
- HR check after set 2
- Target HR: Peak 110–120 bpm; recover to <100 bpm within 2 min

**Cues:**
- "Chest up; knees track over toes"
- "Exhale forcefully as you drive up"
- "Full range of motion; control the descent"

**Notes:** If 60 kg feels too heavy (RPE >6/10), reduce to 55 kg. If RPE is 3/10, increase to 65 kg next week.

---

**2. Barbell Deadlift (Secondary Lower-Body Compound)**

*Setup:* Bar over mid-foot; hip-width stance; neutral spine; shoulders slightly in front of bar; overhand or mixed grip.

*Breathing:* Inhale at top; exhale forcefully on drive-up.

*Tempo:* 2 sec down (controlled), 1 sec up (explosive).

**Warm-up sets:**
- 1 × 5 @ 45 kg (empty bar)
- 1 × 3 @ 60 kg

**Working sets:**
- 3 sets × 8 reps @ 70 kg
- Rest 2.5 min between sets
- HR check after set 2
- Target HR: Peak 110–120 bpm; recover to <100 bpm within 2 min

**Cues:**
- "Drive hips forward; full lockout at top"
- "Exhale forcefully as you drive up"
- "Neutral spine; slight chest lift"

**Notes:** If 70 kg feels too heavy (RPE >6/10), reduce to 65 kg. If RPE is 3/10, increase to 75 kg next week.

---

**3. Leg Press (Accessory Lower-Body)**

- 3 sets × 12 reps @ 50 kg
- Rest 90 sec between sets
- Breathing: Exhale on press; controlled descent
- HR: Should stay 100–110 bpm

---

**4. Core Circuit (2 rounds, 75 sec rest between rounds):**
- Plank hold: 40 sec
- Dead bugs: 10 per side
- Glute bridges: 15 reps
- Bird dogs: 8 per side

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Quad, hamstring, hip flexor, calf stretches (45 sec each)

**Session A Totals:**
- **Squat volume:** 40 reps @ 60 kg
- **Deadlift volume:** 24 reps @ 70 kg
- **Leg press volume:** 36 reps @ 50 kg
- **Total lower-body reps:** 100
- **HR profile:** Peaks 110–120 bpm during compounds; recovers well
- **RPE:** 5/10 overall
- **Caloric expenditure:** ~300–350 kcal

---

### Session B (Tuesday) – Steady-State Aerobic (5K Pace Building)

**Duration:** 40 min | **Intensity:** Moderate (RPE 4/10)

**Warm-up (5 min):**
- 2 min easy treadmill walk/jog (HR 85–90 bpm)
- Dynamic stretching (leg swings, arm circles, torso rotations)

**Main (30 min):**

**Steady-State Aerobic Block:**
- **Modality:** Treadmill (preferred for 5K training)
- **Duration:** 25 min continuous
- **Pace:** 5.5–6.0 km/h (10:00–10:54 min/km) — conversational pace
- **HR target:** 100–110 bpm (RPE 4/10)
- **Incline:** 0–1% (flat)
- **HR monitoring:** Check every 5 min; adjust speed if HR exceeds 115 bpm
- **Breathing:** Rhythmic, nasal breathing preferred; no breath-holding

**Cue:** "Find a pace you could sustain for 30 minutes; you should be able to speak short sentences."

**Distance:** 25 min @ 5.5–6.0 km/h = 2.3–2.5 km

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- 2 min easy walking
- 3 min stretching (hamstrings, quads, hip flexors, calves)

**Session B Totals:**
- **Duration:** 40 min
- **Distance:** 2.3–2.5 km
- **HR:** Steady 100–110 bpm
- **RPE:** 4/10
- **Caloric expenditure:** ~200–250 kcal

---

### Session C (Wednesday) – Upper-Body Compounds + Arms

**Duration:** 55 min | **Intensity:** Moderate (RPE 5/10)

**Warm-up (10 min):**
- 2 min treadmill walk
- Band pull-aparts: 2 × 12
- Light dumbbell rows: 2 × 10 @ 4 kg
- Arm circles, shoulder rolls, scapular wall slides

**Main (40 min):**

**1. Barbell Bench Press (Primary Upper-Body Push Compound)**

*Setup:* Bar across mid-chest; grip slightly wider than shoulder-width; feet flat on floor; slight arch in lower back; shoulder blades retracted.

*Breathing:* Inhale as you lower; exhale forcefully as you press up.

*Tempo:* 2 sec down (controlled), 1 sec up (explosive).

**Warm-up sets:**
- 1 × 8 @ 20 kg (empty bar)
- 1 × 6 @ 30 kg
- 1 × 4 @ 40 kg

**Working sets:**
- 4 sets × 10 reps @ 45 kg
- Rest 2.5 min between sets
- HR check after set 2
- Target HR: Peak 110–120 bpm; recover to <100 bpm within 2 min

**Cues:**
- "Full range of motion; bar touches chest lightly"
- "Exhale forcefully as you press up"
- "Never hold breath during the press"

**Notes:** If 45 kg feels too heavy (RPE >6/10), reduce to 40 kg. If RPE is 3/10, increase to 50 kg next week.

---

**2. Barbell Bent-Over Row (Secondary Upper-Body Pull Compound)**

*Setup:* Bar over mid-foot; hip-width stance; hip hinge ~45°; slight knee bend; neutral spine; shoulders slightly in front of bar; overhand grip.

*Breathing:* Inhale as you lower; exhale forcefully as you pull.

*Tempo:* 2 sec down (controlled), 1 sec up (explosive).

**Warm-up sets:**
- 1 × 5 @ 20 kg (empty bar)
- 1 × 3 @ 30 kg

**Working sets:**
- 3 sets × 8 reps @ 40 kg
- Rest 2.5 min between sets
- HR check after set 2
- Target HR: Peak 110–120 bpm; recover to <100 bpm within 2 min

**Cues:**
- "Drive elbows back; squeeze shoulder blades"
- "Bar touches lower chest"
- "Exhale forcefully as you pull up"

**Notes:** If 40 kg feels too heavy (RPE >6/10), reduce to 35 kg. If RPE is 3/10, increase to 45 kg next week.

---

**3. Lat Pulldown (Accessory Upper-Body Pull)**

- 3 sets × 12 reps @ 30 kg
- Rest 90 sec between sets
- Breathing: Exhale on pull; controlled ascent
- Cue: "Chest up; pull elbows down and back"

---

**4. Arm Superset (2 rounds, 75 sec rest):**
- Dumbbell bicep curls: 12 reps @ 5 kg per hand
- Dumbbell tricep extensions: 12 reps @ 5 kg per hand
- Breathing: Exhale on exertion; controlled eccentric

---

**Cool-down (5 min):**
- Chest, shoulder, tricep, bicep stretches (45 sec each)

**Session C Totals:**
- **Bench press volume:** 40 reps @ 45 kg
- **Bent-over row volume:** 24 reps @ 40 kg
- **Lat pulldown volume:** 36 reps @ 30 kg
- **Arm volume:** 48 reps @ 5 kg
- **Total upper-body reps:** 148
- **HR:** Peaks 110–120 bpm during compounds
- **RPE:** 5/10 overall
- **Caloric expenditure:** ~300–350 kcal

**Interval Structure (Week 1):**
- **Warm-up:** 5 min easy (HR 95–100 bpm)
- **Work intervals:** 3 min @ moderate intensity (HR 110–115 bpm, RPE 5/10)

- Elliptical: 5 min, HR 110–115 bpm, RPE 5/10
